# Guillaume, 2026-11-17, seat t8-fix-plugin-upgrade-and-working-failure-2611170842 (voice transcription, verbatim)

Context: in this session the wheel MCP server of the miadi-chronicle-episode-kit plugin failed to reconnect in Jerry's mailing seat (f1-t6-mailing-and-prep-atelier-jerry-2611131123). Cause: the host-wide MWCV variable (4.27.10) shadowed the plugin pin (4.27.15) and the npx cache for 4.27.10 was broken. Fix: kit 0.3.61 (commit 3619785) reads MIADI_CHRONICLE_MW_MCP instead of MWCV. A review of the 12 open PRs of jgwill/miadi-orchestration-kit followed.

---

Okay, there's a lot of implications on the future steps, and I think that this is not a human stretch to actually work with that much relation. I'm not looking basically at what you actually did, and it's great, you know, you remove the dependency for the variable, which is really great. After that, it's okay that we left the variable there because there are other configuration on the systems that are using it, and we will not search, we will not fix anything. It's just we're jumping into a new way of working with the plugin, and it seems like you resolved all of that. So we'll want to report by email. You know, if you look at use the factory email in the recent threads, that needs this plugin to work fine with all of the actual commands. We'll need to report on these fixes, you know, pretty much like we write platform upgrades or fixes, you know, this file that we put at the root of a repository, like release notes that by version that nobody reads. But knowing that human participant and agents that you might observe emails when they receive it, they're going to be able to interpret these release notes, and it's going to give us an example of something that we would publish once or twice a week. And if I go back to the PR review, you know, it could be part of your actual release note, which PR are actually, you know, going on. I would say the next release, basically, so it would create a very interesting narrative form to the actual implementation. So I think I'm going to send you this message right away, like this, and you're going to do all of that and come back. I'm still going to read, you know, I'm at that section where it says ready after a read, and I see that there's a, you know, the skill onset performance seems to be ready, and it would be good to have a few paragraphs that expresses in this release note. There would be an additional section that would be called the road ahead, in which, you know, what we're basically going to do in this session and we're envisioning to do is going to be part of that section. And also, because we're doing something very important, I think it should be a plugin where the skill of drafting a release notes with the road ahead is a plot thread key moment in terms of narrative beat inside of a session such as the one I'm doing with you right now, that we will want to use the plugin to actually write to the community to whom is relevant. And you could also fill a new issue inside of the factory, because we will want to develop a mailing list or something through which some type of users that we gave them the adequate role of being, of subscribing to such mailing lists, so they would receive the release notes as readers. And there would be another permission that we will want, which is when the user that have that permission actually received a release note with the road ahead. When the factory received an email from them, she's going to consider their feedback as influencing the sessions and the ceremonies that will work on the roads ahead.
